title: Help getting started
author: No_Ebb3423
selftext:
Hello all, I recently got into ai trading mainly by using Hermes & connecting it to alpaca paper trader & also Polymarket.

I’ve consistently been at a loss. Do you guys recommend any YouTube videos to watch, books, or any learning materials to get better results? Because I’d like to get into ai trading see if it could pay off my expensive local LLM hardware addiction. 😂 But everything I’ve tried has consistently failed.

Any tips, tricks, recommendations would be greatly appreciated. I’ve even considered going back to school for a b.s. in finance.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Losing on paper at first is common, and it's useful that you're seeing it before real money is involved. Instead of finding more material, I'd cut it down to one simple written rule and compare its results with just holding, or with random entries, after fees and spreads. Prediction markets and short-term trades are the hardest places to start, because the costs take a big share of small edges. A degree isn't needed to learn this, since keeping a log and testing one change at a time teaches most of it. Cymetica's Backtest Labs has a fee setting and a held out stretch of data for testing a rule before you run it live.

comments.author: BenchifyAppDNS
comments.body:
AI trading isn't easy. So many strategies work one day but not another. If you want to go into the woods, I can recommend a couple of books and papers:

* ***Advances in Financial Machine Learning*** **by Dr. Marcos López de Prado**   This is the industry standard for applying ML to financial time series. Pay close attention to:  
   * **The Triple-Barrier Method:** How to label data based on profit-taking, stop-loss, and holding periods rather than fixed time horizons.
   * **Meta-Labeling:** Using ML to determine trade sizing and signal probability rather than simple directional bets.
   * **Purged & Embargoed K-Fold Cross-Validation:** Preventing data leakage in overlapping time series.
* ***Machine Learning for Algorithmic Trading*** **by Stefan Jansen**   A practical guide using Python to build end-to-end data pipelines, backtesting frameworks, and ML pipelines.

# Empirical Asset Pricing & Market Frictions

* **Fama & French (1992) –** ***The Cross-Section of Expected Stock Returns***   Understand factor investing (Value, Size, Quality, Momentum). AI should complement structural risk factors rather than attempt to invent signals out of thin air.
* **Shleifer & Vishny (1997) –** ***The Limits of Arbitrage***   Learn how market frictions, liquidity crises, and institutional constraints cause systematic mispricings.
